newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine workers march to endorse Dec. 26 strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine workers march to endorse Dec. 26 strike.

text.p: Some 2,000 Argentine workers on Monday evening marched from the National Congress to the building that houses the president's offices, in a show of support for a 24-hour strike called for Thursday.

"Let's keep fighting until we're able to change this sinister government," Victor de Gennaro, a trade union leader, told the crowd during the peaceful protest, which ended at Government House in the Argentine capital.

The strike on Thursday was called by the General Labor Confederation (CGT) to protest presidential decrees curtailing the wage-bargaining power of unions and their monopoly over health insurance schemes. The decrees were signed last week.
President Carlos Menem on Monday dismissed the threatened strike as a "tourist" ploy, saying the unions just wanted an extra day's holiday after Christmas.
The government says the labor reforms will help reduce Argentina's 17.3 percent unemployment.
The strike would mark the third staged in the past five months to protest Menem's economic liberalization policies.
